chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ali, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: May Allah have mercy on a servant who remained chaste and self-sufficient, and refrained from begging, for indeed it hastens humiliation in this world and the next, and people will not be of any avail to him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social consequence of refraining from begging according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that *al-mas'alah* (begging) is not merely a financial act but a spiritual vulnerability that accelerates *al-dhull* (humiliation) in both realms. This teaching aligns with the Shia emphasis on *al-istighna* (self-sufficiency) as a means of preserving dignity and avoiding the dependency that weakens one's standing before Allah and people.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “May Allah shower mercy on His virtuous and pious servant who did not beg inspite of difficulties even though he was troubled in this world and his desires were not fulfilled.”
